records.original_response: Once upon a time, a man had a donkey and a bull. One evening, after the bull had ploughed the field, he came home tired and complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. The next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough; two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response:
The donkey and the bull

Once upon a time in a certain village there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response: Once upon a time, a man had a donkey and a bull. One evening, after the bull had ploughed the field, he came home tired and complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. The next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough; two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response:
The donkey and the bull

Once upon a time in a certain village there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response:
The donkey and the bull

Once upon a time in a certain village there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

---

**Translation of the target sentence:**

**Tsez:** Nełƛ'ay soder yiłade idu yig, ʕa

records.original_response:
The donkey and the bull

Once upon a time in a certain village there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response:
The donkey and the bull

Once upon a time in a certain village there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response: That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response: Once upon a time, a man had a donkey and a bull. One evening, after ploughing the field, the bull came home tired and complained to the donkey. "My master has no pity on me now," he said. "What should I do?" The donkey felt sorry for him and gave him advice: "Pretend to be sick." The next day, the bull pretended to be ill and refused to eat. His master, seeing this, took the donkey instead to plough the field. The donkey went for two days, grew weak, and realized that following such advice brings harm to oneself. Later, the master, believing the bull was dying, slaughtered him. This is why the Tsez people say: "The animal that fears work will die under the dagger."

records.original_response:
The donkey and the bull

Once upon a time in a certain village there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response:
The donkey and the bull

Once upon a time in a certain village there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

**English translation:**
"Once upon a time, there was a man who had a donkey and a bull. One evening, after the bull had ploughed the field, he came home tired and complained to the donkey: 'My dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do?' The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice: 'You should pretend to be sick.' The next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretended to be sick and did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough; two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: 'The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.'"

records.original_response:
The donkey and the bull

Once upon a time in a certain village there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response: Once upon a time, in a certain village, there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response:
The donkey and the bull

Once upon a time in a certain village there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response: There once was a man who had a donkey and a bull. One evening, after the bull had ploughed the field, he came home tired and complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response:
The donkey and the bull

Once upon a time in a certain village there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response:
The donkey and the bull

Once upon a time in a certain village there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.original_response: The donkey and the bull once lived together in a village. One evening, after the bull had ploughed the field until he was exhausted, he complained to the donkey, saying, "My master has no pity for me now; what should I do?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him this advice: "Pretend to be sick." The next day, the bull, following the donkey's advice, pretended to be ill and refused to eat. His master, without even speaking a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, and two days later he grew weak. He then said that advice given to a person brings evil upon oneself. Later, the master, claiming that the bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. This is why the Tsez people say: "The animal that fears work will die under the dagger."

records.original_response:
The donkey and the bull

Once upon a time in a certain village there lived a man. That man had a donkey and a bull. Once, when the bull came home tired after having ploughed the field till evening, he complained to the donkey. "Dear donkey, I am dead tired. My master has no pity on me now. What should I do now?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice. He said he should pretend to be sick. Next day, the bull, as the donkey had said, pretending to be sick, did not eat. The master, without even saying a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, two days he went. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: The animal that is afraid of work will die under the dagger.

records.reference: The old man said to him: "Hey, my son, you slaughtered the one and only ram; and you made bread from the wheat that remained in your home; so what are you planning to do now?"
records.original_response: Once upon a time, there was a man who had a donkey and a bull. One evening, when the bull came home tired from ploughing, he complained to the donkey, saying, "My master has no pity on me now. What should I do?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him this advice: "Tomorrow, pretend to be sick and do not eat." The next day, the bull, as the donkey had advised, pretended to be ill and refused to eat. The master, without even speaking a word, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough; two days he continued. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: "The animal that fears work will die under the dagger."

records.original_response: Once upon a time, a man had a donkey and a bull. One evening, after ploughing, the bull complained to the donkey, saying, "My master has no pity on me now; I am dead tired. What should I do?" The donkey felt sorry for the bull and gave him a piece of advice: "Pretend to be sick." The next day, the bull, as the donkey had advised, pretended to be ill and did not eat. The master, without even speaking, took the donkey instead of the bull to plough. One day the donkey went to plough, and for two days he continued. The donkey grew weak. He said that advice given to a person brings evil to oneself. Later, the master, saying that this bull was now dying, suddenly slaughtered it. That is why the Tsez people say: "The animal that fears work will die under the dagger."
